title: lint: liveness-properties flattens one level of `children`, but 40 grandchild ledger rows carry a status (e.g. `dashboard/widgets.chartConfig.*`), so they are never graded
body:
Filed by domain:spec seat 2 (account zhuangjianguo, session_01RyMY3prh9GRva1Tt37Di3i). It comes from an out-of-scope finding in the #25767 os-dev-report ([comment 6417406701](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/25767#issuecomment-6417406701)). Not a claim.

## Finding

`packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.ts` walks a ledger as top-level props plus **one** level of `children`: `loadWarnMap` at `:129`/`:149` and the status census at `:350`. The coverage seam's docblock (`:303-306`) states the depth as measured: "423 top-level and 285 child rows carry a status, zero grandchildren do".

That is no longer true on `origin/main` (`d1ea2363f`). Walking `packages/spec/liveness/*.json` three levels down finds **40** grandchild rows with a `status`. Examples:

- `dashboard.json`: `widgets.chartConfig.type` = `dead`, plus `widgets.chartConfig.title` / `subtitle` / … = `live`
- `app.json`: `navigation.dataSource.provider` / `read` / `path` = `planned`

None of these rows reaches the warn map or the status census. So a `dead` grandchild that opts into `authorWarn` would never warn, and a new status word used only at grandchild depth would slip past the #14057 vocabulary guard.

Reproduction (repo root):

```
node -e 'const fs=require("fs"),p="packages/spec/liveness/";let n=0;for(const f of fs.readdirSync(p).filter(f=>f.endsWith(".json"))){const j=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(p+f));for(const e of Object.values(j.properties||{}))for(const c of Object.values(e?.children||{}))for(const g of Object.values(c?.children||{}))if(g?.status)n++}console.log(n)'
```

## Done when

Either the walker descends every `children` level, and a test pins that a grandchild `dead` row with `authorWarn` produces the warning, or a test fails while any grandchild row carries a `status` and the 40 rows are moved to a depth the walker reads. The `:303-306` count is re-measured either way.
